title: You don’t get to choose whether there’s a war.
paragraphs:
You don’t get to choose whether there’s a war.
Only which side wins.

One war drains you.
Feeds your impulses.
Makes excuses feel logical.
Keeps you “almost” disciplined.

The other war costs you comfort.
But it builds clarity.
Strength.
Peace that doesn’t depend on mood.

Galatians 5:17 says the flesh desires what is contrary to the Spirit.
Meaning this tension you feel?
It’s not weakness.
It’s evidence of conflict.

The battle isn’t out there.
It’s in what you scroll.
What you tolerate.
What you do when no one is watching.

Avoiding the fight doesn’t create peace.
It just hands victory to the flesh.

And the war you avoid today
will own you tomorrow.

Some of you aren’t tired.
You’re spiritually undisciplined and calling it exhaustion.

But here’s the good news—
the Spirit doesn’t require perfection.
He requires surrender.

And surrender is a decision.
Daily.
Sometimes hourly.
🤍 If you’re done losing silent battles…
